lyrics:
[Intro: fingerpicked acoustic guitar, soft dobro]

[Verse 1: warm male voice, storytelling]
Granny had a shoebox and a ballpoint pen
Every picture that we took, she'd turn it over and then
She'd lick her thumb and squint and say who and where and when
I asked her why. She didn't look up. She said

[Chorus: harmony joins, gentle full band]
"Write it on the back
Who's that baby, whose front porch, what year
'Cause one day you'll be holding this
And nobody who knows will still be here
Say the names while there's somebody to ask
And write it on the back"

[Verse 2: voice and band, easy]
She said, "Call your brother, even when you're sore
Learn one good pie and how to fix a door
Sit with the old ones, let 'em tell it twice
The second time through is where they hide the good advice"

[Chorus: harmony joins, gentle full band]
"Write it on the back
Who's that baby, whose front porch, what year
'Cause one day you'll be holding this
And nobody who knows will still be here
Say the names while there's somebody to ask
And write it on the back"

[Bridge: dobro and voice, hushed]
We buried her in April with her reading glasses on
I got the shoebox. Every face has got a name.
She's not gone.

[Final Chorus: full band, harmony close]
So I write it on the back
"That's your granny, that's her porch, that's you, age three"
'Cause one day you'll be holding this
And you won't have to guess, like me
I say the names to my kids, just like she asked
And I write it on the back

[Outro: guitar, a pen clicking]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 88 BPM, 4/4, C major. Gentle and steady, like someone talking while their hands are busy.

VOICE: Male, warm and plain, in the middle of his range, telling it without drama. A second, older-sounding voice sings harmony on the choruses. The bridge is close to speech.

INSTRUMENTS: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar, dobro, mandolin, upright bass, brushed drums entering at the first chorus, a soft fiddle line in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and dobro. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:42 Chorus 1. 1:12 Verse 2. 1:40 Chorus 2. 2:10 Bridge, hushed. 2:32 Final chorus, in his own words. 3:06 Outro, guitar and a pen click at 3:26.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Acoustic, warm and close: wood and strings, soft low end, nothing electric.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'She's not gone' at 2:28.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original's advice is to buy land. This one's is free and more urgent in an age of ten thousand unlabelled phone pictures: name the faces while someone still can.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Curious child, listening, loss, carrying it on.
